This name inspires a sense of devotion, unity, and oneness with the divine, invoking a spiritual connection and inner peace.

historical_references.reference:
The temple at Ekamansh was built by King Bhagiratha in ancient India, around 6th-5th century BC, as a tribute to Lord Shiva. The temple was believed to be the place where the God appeared to the king after he had brought the river Goddess Ganga down to earth from the heavens.

Reference: History of Ancient India, Volume II. New Delhi: Tarasankar Sarkar.

Reference: Indo-Greek and Indo-Scythian Coins. New Delhi: Oriental Numismatic Company.
